# Copilot instructions - skill index

Auto-generated by scripts/generate-copilot.ps1. Do not edit by hand - edit skills/<name>/SKILL.md instead.

Full skill bodies live in .github/instructions/<name>.instructions.md.

- **ask-matt** - Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.
- **audit-security** - Audit a whole project for security holes against the OWASP Top 10 — a coverage inventory to run before a release, when onboarding, or periodically (not per-PR). Unlike code-review, which gates a single diff, this scans the entire codebase for holes that already exist across Broken Access Control (missing authz, IDOR/BOLA, privilege escalation), Security Misconfiguration (default credentials, leaked stack traces, missing headers, CORS), Software Supply Chain (vulnerable or unpinned dependencies), Cryptographic Failures (weak algorithms, committed keys, unsalted password hashing, disabled cert validation), Injection (SQL/NoSQL/OS-command/ORM/LDAP/template), Authentication Failures (session fixation, unverified JWT claims, user enumeration), Integrity Failures (insecure deserialization), Logging Failures (unlogged events, secrets in logs), and Exceptional Conditions (swallowed errors, fail-open, non-atomic ops). Produces a per-category inventory. For a test-coverage audit use audit-test instead.
- **audit-test** - Audit a whole project's test suite — a coverage inventory to run before a release, when onboarding a codebase, or periodically. Scans the entire codebase (not a single diff) for where testing is thin or missing: pyramid balance (too few unit tests, or a slow top-heavy pile of e2e tests), modules and critical flows with no test at any level, missing test types for the surface that needs them (integration tests that never hit real infrastructure, service boundaries with no contract test, critical flows with no end-to-end test, flaky snapshots), and periodic disciplines a red-green loop can't show (mutation testing, smoke/sanity/regression suites, load/stress/soak/spike performance testing). Reports per-concern gaps ranked by risk. This inventories EXISTING tests — it does not write tests (use tdd), does not review one diff or PR (use code-review), and is not a security audit (use audit-security). Framework- and language-agnostic.
- **codebase-design** - Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- **code-review** - Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along four axes — Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?), Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?), Security (does the diff introduce an OWASP hole — Broken Access Control, Security Misconfiguration, Software Supply Chain, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Authentication Failures, Integrity Failures, Logging Failures, Exceptional Conditions, and other categories as they're added), and Tests (does new/changed behavior ship with a test at the right level, and would a bug fix have a regression test that catches it). Runs the reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- **diagnosing-bugs** - Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- **domain-modeling** - Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- **grilling** - Grill the user relentlessly about a plan, decision, or idea. Use when the user wants to stress-test their thinking, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- **grill-me** - A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design.
- **grill-with-docs** - A relentless interview to sharpen a plan or design, which also creates docs (ADR's and glossary) as we go.
- **handoff** - Compact the current conversation into a handoff document for another agent to pick up.
- **implement** - "Implement a piece of work based on a spec or set of tickets."
- **improve-codebase-architecture** - Scan a codebase for deepening opportunities, present them as a visual HTML report, then grill through whichever one you pick.
- **prototype** - Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- **research** - Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- **resolving-merge-conflicts** - "Use when you need to resolve an in-progress git merge/rebase conflict."
- **setup-matt-pocock-skills** - Configure this repo for the engineering skills — set up its issue tracker, triage label vocabulary, domain doc layout, and test-tool mapping. Run once before first use of the other engineering skills.
- **tdd** - Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- **teach** - Teach the user a new skill or concept, within this workspace.
- **to-issues** - 'Break a plan, spec, or PRD into independently-grabbable issues on the project issue tracker using tracer-bullet vertical slices. Use when the user wants to convert a plan into issues, create implementation tickets, or break down work into issues.'
- **to-prd** - 'Turn the current conversation context into a PRD and publish it to the project issue tracker. Use when the user wants to create a PRD, document a feature, write a product requirements document, or publish a spec from the current context. Do NOT interview the user — synthesize from what is already known.'
- **to-questionnaire** - Turn a decision you can't fully answer into a questionnaire for someone else to fill in.
- **to-spec** - Turn the current conversation into a spec and publish it to the project issue tracker — no interview, just synthesis of what you've already discussed.
- **to-tickets** - Break a plan, spec, or the current conversation into a set of tracer-bullet tickets, each declaring its blocking edges, published to the configured tracker — edges as text in one file per ticket locally, or native blocking links on a real tracker.
- **triage** - Move issues and external PRs through a state machine of triage roles — categorise, verify, grill if needed, and write agent-ready briefs.
- **wait-what** - Stop. That last message did not land — re-pitch it.
- **wayfinder** - Plan a huge chunk of work — more than one agent session can hold — as a shared map of decision tickets on your issue tracker, and resolve them one at a time until the way to the destination is clear.
- **wizard** - Generate an interactive bash wizard that walks a human through steps only they can perform. Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
- **writing-for-agents** - Writing documents for agents. Use when creating or editing skills, or modifying AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
